intro: A fairly quiet day. AI shopping agents keep spreading (Klarna, Zalando) and the Instagram–Amazon links story moves on to what creators actually earn. Rebrandly's merger leads the competitor news.

must_reads.title: Klarna moves further into cashback and affiliate territory with AI shopping agent
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Klarna, a payments company, is moving into cashback and affiliate-style shopping, with an AI shopping assistant in WhatsApp and iMessage across 1.35 million retailers. More big players want to control where people shop, not just how they pay, so the path from a recommendation to a purchase keeps getting more crowded.

must_reads.title: Zalando Extended: What We Know About Zalando’s Agentic Commerce Move
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Zalando is adding other shops' products to its app and plans for its own AI agent to buy them for customers from 2027. Big apps want the whole journey to happen inside them, which makes it harder for the original shop or the creator to stay visible.

must_reads.title: Millions of views, meagre commissions: Can Instagram's Amazon integration make affiliate marketing pay for creators?
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Indian creators say a Reel with two million views earned only a small commission, and that getting viewers to leave one app and buy in another is the hard part. Easier in-app links don't fix low payouts or unclear attribution, so creators still need to see which clicks and sales are really theirs.

must_reads.title: Media Briefing: ChatGPT’s new business hub is an early ‘search console moment’ for publishers
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: ChatGPT's new business hub gives publishers their first real numbers on how often they are mentioned and clicked in ChatGPT. AI answers are becoming a traffic source people can measure, so links that show up and get clicked inside AI tools will matter more.

must_reads.title: Measuring Clicks Is Making ChatGPT Ads Look Like A Bad Bet
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: early ChatGPT ads look weak when judged only on clicks, because people often buy later somewhere else. It is another sign that click-based measurement is breaking in AI shopping, and that tracking needs to follow the buyer across steps and apps.
